reuse/pretrained: Training a ConvNet from scratch takes a lot of labeled data. But networks already trained on ImageNet, over a million photos in a thousand classes, are free to download.
reuse/layers: Their first layers hold filters for edges and colors. Later layers combine those into textures and parts, and the last layer scores the thousand classes.
reuse/swap: To reuse one, keep its layers fixed and replace only the last layer with a new one for your own classes. Here, ten.
reuse/count: With five hundred and twelve features in and ten classes out, the new layer has five thousand one hundred and thirty parameters. Only those are trained.
howmuch/small: With a few hundred images, train just that last layer. Changing millions of weights on so few images would memorize them: overfitting.
howmuch/more: With tens of thousands of images, you can afford more: start from the pretrained weights and fine-tune every layer.
howmuch/lr: Fine-tune with a small learning rate, often ten times smaller than from scratch, so the good pretrained weights move only a little.
howmuch/different: And when your images look nothing like photos, say X-rays, the early layers carry over best: edges are everywhere, while the last layers belong to the old classes.
